**A rolling count changes both when events arrive and when old events expire.** Key transactions by card ID and maintain time-indexed state. Each new transaction enters the relevant ten-minute and 24-hour totals; contributions leave when they pass each window boundary. [1](https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-stable/docs/dev/datastream/operators/windows/)

Keeping every event timestamp supports exact boundaries but uses more state. Minute buckets reduce storage, yet the oldest partial minute creates approximation unless finer detail is retained. Choose that tradeoff explicitly instead of calling a bucketed count exact.

**Event time and arrival time differ.** A late transaction may belong inside a window already processed. Watermarks and an allowed-lateness policy define how to update or reject such records. Deduplicate using transaction IDs so retries do not inflate counts.

Checkpoint state and serve materialized values with timestamps or versions. Define whether the transaction being scored is included, and reconstruct the same definition for training without future events. Monitor hot cards, lag, expiry processing, and recovery. A fast Redis lookup is only trustworthy if the upstream state and time semantics are correct.

**Technical details and references.**

Key the event stream by card ID and maintain time-indexed counts rather than scanning the full transaction history. For exact rolling windows, keep event timestamps/counts in state and expire contributions as event time advances; aggregate equal timestamps or use bounded buckets when approximation is acceptable. Maintain separate 10-minute and 24-hour totals, updating both on each event and expiration. [1](https://nightlies.apache.org/flink/flink-docs-stable/docs/dev/datastream/operators/windows/)

Use watermarks and a stated late-event policy, idempotent transaction IDs, checkpointed state, and retention beyond allowed lateness. Redis can serve materialized values with timestamps/version metadata; the stream processor remains the consistency authority. Define whether the current transaction is included and avoid future information in training features. Minute buckets reduce state but create boundary approximation unless partial buckets retain finer detail. Monitor lag, hot keys, duplicates, and recovery behavior.
